question_text: What are the components of a nucleotide?

insider_note: Three components is the first mark. The second is how they join: base plus sugar is a nucleoside, and a nucleoside with a phosphate is a nucleotide. Naming the purines and pyrimidines completes the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three components
steps.margin_note: All three numbered, with the sugar named for both nucleic acids.
steps.why: These same three parts, repeated millions of times, are all a nucleic acid is made of.
common_mistakes: Naming two components. There are THREE.
Saying the sugar is glucose. It is a PENTOSE: deoxyribose or ribose.
steps.memory_tip: Base, sugar, phosphate: three parts every time.

steps.label: How they are joined
steps.margin_note: Both base classes with their members, then the two definitions.

steps.why: The nucleoside-versus-nucleotide difference is exactly one phosphate group, which is the shortest way to remember both words.
common_mistakes: Confusing nucleoside and nucleotide. The nucleoTide has the phosphaTe.
Listing thymine as a purine. Thymine is a PYRIMIDINE.
steps.memory_tip: Nucleotide has the T of phosphaTe.
